text: Git branching is an important part of modern version control. When developers work on a new feature, they usually create a separate branch instead of changing the main code directly. These feature branches let people test ideas safely without breaking the working project. Once the work is finished, the branch can be merged back into the main branch. Before merging, teams often open a pull request, which allows others to review the changes and discuss them. This simple workflow keeps projects organized and reduces mistakes. By using branches, merges, and pull requests together, teams can collaborate more easily and manage their code with confidence.
